mainTopic: Bones and tendons of an עולה that separate from the meat, whether they go up or become permitted, and a new משנה on things that fall off the מזבח.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a ברייתא: tendons and bones of an עולה go up on the מזבח while attached to the meat, but come down once they separate. The גמרא shows this follows רבי. רבי sets the פסוק 'the whole' against the פסוק 'the flesh and the blood'. The first opinion lets even separated parts go up and uses the 'flesh and blood' פסוק for a different law. רבי זירא and רבה then limit the משנה's rule to parts that separated after the זריקה. Parts that separated before it are permitted for any use, which רבה learns from a גזירה שוה of ״לוֹ יִהְיֶה״ with an אשם. רב אדא בר אהבה challenges רבה from a ברייתא about מעילה, the ברייתא is reread to fit him, and רבי אלעזר is shown to disagree. A new משנה then teaches what happens to things that fall off the מזבח, including the חצות rule for limbs, and says the כבש and the vessels also sanctify. The גמרא starts asking which limbs the חצות rule covers, and the answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Attached parts go up, separated parts come down
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rejects the idea of stripping tendons and bones before burning. It concludes that attached parts go up and separated parts come down, even from the top of the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think the כהן should pull out the tendons and bones and burn only the meat. The פסוק says 'the priest shall burn the whole.' So how do we fit it together? If they are attached, they go up. If they separated, they come down, even if they are already on top of the מזבח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a ברייתא that balances two פסוקים. It concludes that tendons and bones go up only while attached to the meat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'flesh and blood' פסוק could suggest that only meat goes up, so you might strip out the bones first. The words 'את הכל' (the whole) block that idea. The compromise: attached parts go up with the meat, but parts that came loose are taken down.

keyTerms.meaning: One might have thought (opens a wrong assumption)
The verse teaches (brings a פסוק to correct the assumption)
How so? How do we fit the two together?

steps.confusionAlert: 'Come down' applies even if the loose parts are already on top of the מזבח. Being up there does not let them stay.

phrases.english: One might have thought he should remove the tendons and bones,
and bring up only the flesh onto the altar?
The verse teaches:
"And the priest shall burn the whole."
How so?
If attached, they go up;
if they separated, even if they are on top of the altar,
they come down.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a ברייתא begun on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Tendons and bones go up while attached to the meat. Once separated, they come down, even from the top of the מזבח.

steps.title: Which תנא says separated parts come down?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whose opinion it is that separated parts come down.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is the תנא we have heard say that if they separated, they come down?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks who holds the view just stated, that separated parts come down. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule 'פירשו ירדו' is not obvious, because the word 'הכל' could include even loose parts. So the גמרא wants to find the specific תנא who holds it.

keyTerms.meaning: Who is the תנא (which sage holds this)?

phrases.english: Who is the tanna that you have heard
who says: if they separated, they come down?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks who holds the rule concluded in step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the תנא who holds 'פירשו ירדו'.

steps.title: It is רבי, and the first view includes even separated parts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that it is רבי. It begins quoting a ברייתא whose first opinion includes bones, tendons, horns and hooves on the מזבח even after they separate.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is רבי, as a ברייתא teaches: 'And the priest shall burn the whole on the altar.' This comes to include the bones, the tendons, the horns and the hooves, even if they separated.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the view is רבי's. It starts quoting a ברייתא, whose first, unnamed opinion holds the opposite: even separated parts go up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion (the תנא קמא) reads 'הכל' as fully inclusive, so even loose bones and hooves are burned. This sets up the contrast with רבי, whose view comes at the end of the same ברייתא.
steps.confusionAlert: The opinion quoted right after 'דתניא' is NOT רבי's. His opinion comes later, in step 6.

phrases.english: It is Rabbi,
as it is taught in a baraita:
"And the priest shall burn the whole on the altar" —
this comes to include the bones and the tendons
and the horns and the hooves,
even if they separated.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2 and begins quoting the supporting ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The view is רבי's. The ברייתא's first opinion includes even separated parts.

steps.title: What then is the 'flesh and blood' פסוק for?
steps.stepSummary: Within the ברייתא, the first opinion is challenged: if everything goes up, why does the פסוק mention only flesh and blood?
steps.simpleTranslation: But then how do I fulfill the פסוק: 'And you shall offer your burnt offerings, the flesh and the blood'?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא challenges its own first opinion. If even loose bones go up, what does the 'flesh and blood' פסוק come to teach?
steps.deeperAnalysis: That פסוק seems to limit the מזבח to meat and blood. If 'הכל' includes everything, this פסוק looks pointless, so it needs a different job.

keyTerms.meaning: How do I fulfill (what is this verse for)?

phrases.english: But then how do I fulfill:
"And you shall offer your burnt offerings, the flesh and the blood"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the first opinion quoted in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The first opinion's reading of 'הכל' as including even separated parts.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The 'flesh and blood' פסוק would have no purpose.

steps.title: The פסוק teaches about returning burnt pieces
steps.stepSummary: The first opinion answers that the פסוק teaches a different law: burnt meat that falls off the fire goes back on, but burnt tendons and bones do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to tell you: burnt pieces of an עולה you put back, but you do not put back burnt pieces of tendons and bones.
steps.whatsHappening: The first opinion gives the 'flesh and blood' פסוק its own job, about pieces that fall off the fire.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק does not limit what goes up to begin with. It limits what gets returned after partly burning and falling off: meat goes back, tendons and bones do not.
steps.whatToRemember: For the first opinion, everything goes up, even loose parts. The 'flesh and blood' פסוק only limits returning burnt pieces that fell off.

phrases.english: It comes to tell you:
the burnt pieces of a burnt offering you put back,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אַתָּה מַחֲזִיר עִיכּוּלֵי גִּידִין וַעֲצָמוֹת.
phrases.english: but you do not put back burnt pieces of tendons and bones.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the פסוק a different purpose
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The 'flesh and blood' פסוק seemed to limit what may go up at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: It only limits which burnt pieces are returned to the fire.

steps.title: רבי: one פסוק includes, one excludes
steps.stepSummary: רבי sets the two פסוקים against each other. 'הכל' includes, and 'flesh and blood' excludes. He concludes that attached parts go up and separated parts come down.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי says: one פסוק says 'the priest shall burn the whole on the altar', which includes. Another פסוק says 'your burnt offerings, the flesh and the blood', which excludes. How so? If attached, they go up. If they separated, even if they are on top of the מזבח, they come down.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now gives רבי's view. It proves that he is the one who holds 'פירשו ירדו'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי uses the 'flesh and blood' פסוק to limit, not for returning pieces. He splits the two פסוקים: attached parts are included, and separated parts are excluded. His wording matches step 1 exactly, which proves that ברייתא follows רבי.
steps.whatToRemember: The rule 'מחוברין יעלו, פירשו ירדו' belongs to רבי. The first opinion lets even separated parts go up.

phrases.english: Rabbi says:
One verse says:
"And the priest shall burn the whole on the altar" — it included;
and another verse says:
"And you shall offer your burnt offerings, the flesh and the blood" — it excluded.
How so?
If attached, they go up;
if they separated, even if they are on top of the altar,
they come down.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא with רבי's opposing view, which proves the answer of step 3.
steps.raayaObject: That the ruling in step 1 follows רבי.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ending of the ברייתא, where רבי states 'מחוברין יעלו, פירשו ירדו'.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי holds that attached parts go up and separated parts come down.

steps.title: רבי זירא limits the rule to parts that fell downward
steps.stepSummary: Quoting the משנה's rule that separated parts do not go up, רבי זירא says this applies only if they separated downward. If they separated upward, toward the fire, they got closer to being burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: if they separated, they do not go up. רבי זירא said: this was taught only when they separated downward. But if they separated upward, they have come closer to being burned up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה about separated bones and tendons. רבי זירא then limits it to parts that fell away from the fire.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה seemed to say that any separated bone or tendon comes down. רבי זירא adds a condition: only if it moved away from the fire. If it moved toward the fire, it is closer to being burned, so it is treated differently.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught this in the case of… (a limiting formula)

phrases.english: If they separated, they shall not go up, etc.
Rabbi Zeira said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁפֵּירְשׁוּ כְּלַפֵּי מַטָּה,
phrases.english: They taught this only where they separated downward,
but if upward,
they have come closer to being consumed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the ברייתא of רבי back to the next clause of the משנה and limits it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Separated parts come down only if they separated away from the fire. If they separated toward it, they are closer to being burned.

steps.title: How can separated parts ever go up?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי זירא: the משנה clearly says separated parts do not go up, so how can some separated parts go up?
steps.simpleTranslation: And even if they separated, they go up?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי זירא's statement in two short words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה allows only attached parts to go up. רבי זירא seems to let some separated parts go up, which contradicts the משנה's plain wording. This sets up רבה's rereading.

phrases.english: And even if they separated?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי זירא's statement from step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי זירא's claim that parts that separated upward still go up
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה says separated parts do not go up, with no exception for direction.

steps.title: רבה: the real issue is before or after the sprinkling
steps.stepSummary: רבה rereads רבי זירא. The משנה's rule is needed only for parts that separated after the זריקה. Parts that separated before the זריקה are permitted by the זריקה for any use, even knife handles.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: this is what he means. They taught this only when they separated after the sprinkling. But if they separated before the sprinkling, the sprinkling comes and permits them, even to make knife handles out of them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers the challenge by explaining רבי זירא in a new way. The difference is about timing, not up or down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the parts were still attached at the time of the זריקה, they were fit for the מזבח. So the משנה needs to tell us that once they separate, they come down. If they were already separated before the זריקה, they never belonged to the מזבח at all. The זריקה makes them fully permitted, like the hide of a עולה.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he means (rereading a statement)
Sprinkling of the blood on the מזבח

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the parts separated before זריקה go up on the מזבח. The opposite is true: they never go up, and they are even allowed for ordinary use.

phrases.english: Rabba said, this is what he is saying:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁפֵּירְשׁוּ לְאַחַר זְרִיקָה,
phrases.english: They taught this only where they separated after the sprinkling,
but if they separated before the sprinkling,
the sprinkling comes and permits them,
even to make knife handles out of them.
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the word in square brackets is the corrected wording. Both mean handles.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 8 by rereading רבי זירא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the statement (הכי קאמר): changing the dividing line from direction to timing
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי זירא seemed to say that parts that separated upward still go up on the מזבח.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה's rule is needed only for parts that separated after the זריקה. Parts that separated before it are permitted for any use.

steps.title: רבה's source: the גזירה שוה of ״לוֹ יִהְיֶה״
steps.stepSummary: רבה relies on רבי יוחנן quoting רבי ישמעאל. ״לוֹ יִהְיֶה״ is written by both עולה and אשם. Just as an אשם's bones are permitted, so too are a עולה's bones.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds like what רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי ישמעאל: ״לוֹ יִהְיֶה״ is said about a burnt offering, and ״לוֹ יִהְיֶה״ is said about a guilt offering. Just as the guilt offering's bones are permitted, so too the burnt offering's bones are permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows where רבה gets his idea that the bones can be permitted for ordinary use.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same words, ״לוֹ יִהְיֶה״, appear by עולה and by אשם, so we learn one from the other (גזירה שוה). An אשם's bones are not burned on the מזבח and become permitted. So a עולה's bones that are not going on the מזבח are permitted too.

keyTerms.meaning: Burnt offering, burned entirely on the מזבח

phrases.english: He holds in line with this,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל:
phrases.english: that Rabbi Yoḥanan said in the name of Rabbi Yishmael:
"He shall have" is stated regarding a burnt offering,
and "He shall have" is stated regarding a guilt offering;
just as with a guilt offering, its bones are permitted,
so too with a burnt offering, its bones are permitted.
phrases.notes: Some versions say "bones" (round brackets); the corrected wording says "its bones" (square brackets).

steps.triggerLanguage: סָבַר לַהּ כִּי הָא דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for רבה's claim in step 9 that the זריקה permits the bones.
steps.raayaObject: רבה's ruling that bones separated before זריקה are permitted for any use
steps.raayaSupportSource: The גזירה שוה ״לוֹ יִהְיֶה״ between עולה and אשם, from רבי יוחנן in the name of רבי ישמעאל

steps.title: Why the comparison holds: the words are extra
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes the ״לוֹ יִהְיֶה״ words are free (מופנה). Otherwise one could object that an אשם is different because its meat is permitted. The extra words protect the גזירה שוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The words are free. For if they were not free, one could object: what about an אשם? Its meat is permitted! But ״לוֹ יִהְיֶה״ is written as extra.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא protects the גזירה שוה from an obvious objection by pointing out that the words are extra in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אשם's meat is eaten, so maybe that is why its bones are permitted. The meat of a עולה is all burned, so the comparison could seem weak. But since ״לוֹ יִהְיֶה״ is extra by עולה, it is there to be used for the גזירה שוה, and such an objection cannot knock it down.

keyTerms.meaning: Free, set aside for teaching a גזירה שוה
What about X, since it has a special feature (form of objection)

steps.whatToRemember: Bones or tendons attached at the time of זריקה go up, but come down if they separate afterward. If they separated before זריקה, they never go up and are fully permitted, learned from the free ״לוֹ יִהְיֶה״ גזירה שוה with אשם.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how a גזירה שוה built on extra words survives a difference between the two cases being compared.

phrases.english: They are free;
phrases.notes: The words ״לוֹ יִהְיֶה״ are extra, so they're free to be used for this comparison.

phrases.english: for if they were not free, one could object:
What about a guilt offering? Its meat is permitted!
"He shall have" is written as extra.

steps.triggerLanguage: מוּפְנֵי; דְּאִי לָא מוּפְנֵי – אִיכָּא לְמִיפְרַךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends the גזירה שוה of step 10 against a possible objection.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Free words (מופנה) block the objection to the comparison
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The comparison could be rejected because an אשם's meat is eaten, while a עולה's is not.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since ״לוֹ יִהְיֶה״ is extra, the גזירה שוה stands despite the difference.

steps.title: A ברייתא says a עולה's bones always carry מעילה
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה quotes a ברייתא. Bones of offerings whose meat is eaten carry מעילה before the זריקה but not after it. A עולה's bones carry מעילה always. This seems to contradict רבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה objects: The bones of קדשים carry מעילה before the זריקה and do not carry מעילה after it. But the bones of a עולה always carry מעילה!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר אהבה brings a ברייתא to attack רבה's rule that a עולה's bones can become permitted. The ברייתא seems to say a עולה's bones never become permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה said bones of a עולה that separated before the זריקה are permitted by the זריקה. The ברייתא says a עולה's bones carry מעילה 'always,' which sounds like it covers every case. If they always carry מעילה, the זריקה never permits them, and רבה is contradicted.

keyTerms.meaning: One is liable for מְעִילָה, the misuse of הקדש
Sprinkling the blood of the offering on the מזבח

phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava raises an objection:
The bones of sacrificial animals,
phrases.notes: Here this means offerings whose meat is eaten, like a חטאת or an אשם.

phrases.english: before the sprinkling, one is liable for misuse with them;
after the sprinkling, one is not liable for misuse with them.
But those of a burnt offering, one is always liable for misuse with them!
phrases.notes: 'Always' sounds like it means both before and after the זריקה, which is the problem for רבה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבה's rule from step 9, which steps 10-11 had just supported
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's ruling that bones of a עולה that separated before the זריקה become permitted
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says a עולה's bones carry מעילה 'always,' which implies the זריקה never permits them

steps.title: Rereading the ברייתא to fit רבה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the ברייתא. A עולה's bones that separated before the זריקה carry no מעילה. Only bones that separated after the זריקה carry מעילה forever.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say it like this: A עולה's bones that separated before the זריקה carry no מעילה. If they separated after the זריקה, they carry מעילה forever.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבה by reading the ברייתא in a new way. The word 'always' is limited to bones that separated after the זריקה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא now splits the עולה case by timing, just as רבה did. Bones that separated before the זריקה were permitted by the זריקה, so there is no מעילה. Bones that were still attached at the זריקה were fit for the מזבח, so if they separate afterward they stay holy forever.

keyTerms.meaning: Say, meaning read the source this way instead
They separated, meaning the bones came apart from the animal

steps.confusionAlert: This feels backwards. You might expect earlier separation to be stricter. But bones that were already loose at the זריקה were not meant for the מזבח, so the זריקה permits them. Bones still attached at the זריקה became part of what goes on the מזבח, so if they come off afterward they stay holy.

phrases.english: Say: And those of a burnt offering,
if they separated before the sprinkling,
one is not liable for misuse with them;
if after the sprinkling, one is always liable for misuse with them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אדא בר אהבה's challenge by rereading the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא means a עולה's bones carry מעילה in every case
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Always' applies only to bones that separated after the זריקה. Bones that separated before it carry no מעילה, as רבה said.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר holds the opposite view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that רבה disagrees with רבי אלעזר. רבי אלעזר says bones that separated before the זריקה carry מעילה. Bones that separated after the זריקה may not be used, but carry no מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This disagrees with רבי אלעזר. רבי אלעזר said: If they separated before the זריקה, they carry מעילה. If they separated after the זריקה, one may not benefit from them, but there is no מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that רבי אלעזר rules differently from רבה about a עולה's bones, and quotes רבי אלעזר's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר flips רבה's timing. For him, bones that separated before the זריקה are not permitted by it, so they carry מעילה. Bones that separated after the זריקה were permitted, so there is no מעילה, but one still may not use them.

keyTerms.meaning: It disagrees, meaning this view argues with another

steps.whatToRemember: רבה: bones that separated before the זריקה are permitted, and after it they carry מעילה forever. רבי אלעזר: bones that separated before the זריקה carry מעילה, and after it there is no מעילה, but one still may not use them.

phrases.english: And this disagrees with Rabbi Elazar;
phrases.notes: 'This' is רבה's view, as the ברייתא was just read to fit him.

phrases.english: as Rabbi Elazar said:
if they separated before the sprinkling, one is liable for misuse with them;

phrases.aramaic: לְאַחַר זְרִיקָה – לֹא נֶהֱנִין וְלֹא מוֹעֲלִין.
phrases.english: after the sprinkling, one may not benefit from them, but one is not liable for misuse.
phrases.notes: From the Torah they are permitted, so there is no מעילה. The ban on using them is a rule of חכמים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending רבה, the גמרא notes that רבי אלעזר holds the opposite view
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אלעזר: a עולה's bones that separated before the זריקה carry מעילה. If they separated after it, one may not benefit from them, but there is no מעילה.

steps.title: What happens to things that fall off the altar
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that disqualified offerings and embers that fall off the מזבח are not put back. Limbs of a kosher עולה are put back only if they fell before חצות, and only then do they carry מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: All the disqualified offerings that fell off the altar are not put back. Likewise an ember that fell off the altar is not put back. Limbs that fell off the altar before midnight are put back, and one is liable for misusing them. After midnight they are not put back, and there is no liability for misusing them.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It tells us which things that fell off the מזבח get put back, and when the limbs of an עולה still carry מעילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Disqualified offerings stay on the מזבח only because they already went up, so once they fall off there is no reason to return them. Limbs of a kosher עולה must burn, so before חצות they are returned and still carry מעילה. After חצות their מצוה is considered done, so they are not returned and carry no מעילה.

keyTerms.meaning: Were dislodged, popped off (from the altar fire)
Limbs of a sacrifice that are burned on the altar
Midnight, the cutoff time for burning the night's limbs
One is liable for מעילה, the misuse of הקדש

steps.confusionAlert: There are two separate groups here. The disqualified offerings are never put back. The kosher limbs depend on whether they fell before or after חצות.

phrases.english: MISHNA: And all of them that were dislodged
phrases.notes: "All of them" means the disqualified offerings from the earlier משנה, the ones that are not taken down once they have gone up.

and likewise, an ember that was dislodged

Limbs that were dislodged from on top of the altar
before midnight — he puts them back, and one is liable for misusing them;

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ וְכוּלָּן שֶׁפָּקְעוּ מֵעַל גַּבֵּי הַמִּזְבֵּחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the discussion of מעילה on bones in Steps 12-14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Disqualified offerings and embers that fall off are not returned. Kosher limbs are returned and carry מעילה before חצות, but not after.

steps.title: The ramp and the vessels also sanctify
steps.stepSummary: The משנה adds that the כבש and the כלי שרת sanctify what is fit for them, just like the מזבח does.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just as the altar sanctifies what is fit for it, so too the ramp sanctifies. Just as the altar and the ramp sanctify what is fit for them, so too the vessels sanctify.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה widens the earlier rule. It teaches that the כבש and the כלי שרת also give holiness to things fit for them, not only the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule that once something goes up it does not come down is not limited to the top of the מזבח. Something fit for the מזבח that reaches the כבש is also held there. Something placed in a כלי שרת becomes sanctified in the same way.

keyTerms.meaning: The ramp leading up to the מזבח
Service vessels (כלי שרת) of the בית המקדש

steps.whatToRemember: The מזבח, the כבש and the כלי שרת all sanctify what is fit for them.

phrases.aramaic: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁהַמִּזְבֵּחַ מְקַדֵּשׁ אֶת הָרָאוּי לוֹ,
phrases.english: Just as the altar sanctifies what is fit for it,
so too, the ramp sanctifies.
Just as the altar and the ramp
sanctify what is fit for them,
so too, the vessels sanctify.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁהַמִּזְבֵּחַ מְקַדֵּשׁ אֶת הָרָאוּי לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה by extending the power to sanctify to the כבש and the כלי שרת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כבש and the כלי שרת sanctify what is fit for them, like the מזבח.

steps.title: Which limbs is the midnight rule talking about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה's חצות rule with a dilemma. If the limbs still have substance, they should go back even after חצות. If they have none, they should not go back even before חצות.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If the limbs still have substance, then even after midnight they should be put back! If they have no substance, then even before midnight they should not be put back!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what case the משנה means when it splits the limbs by before and after חצות. It shows that both possible readings seem to make the time of night irrelevant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Limbs that are still real meat need to burn, so the time should not matter. Limbs that are already ash need nothing more, so again the time should not matter. Either way, the line at חצות looks pointless.

keyTerms.meaning: What are the circumstances? What case is this?
Substance; something still solid and not yet burned up
They do not have in them

phrases.english: GEMARA: What are the circumstances?
If they have substance —
then even after midnight, too, he should put them back!
If they have no substance —
then even before midnight, he should not put them back either!

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי דָּמֵי? אִי דְּאִית בְּהוּ מַמָּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the חצות distinction in Step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that limbs are returned before חצות but not after.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Whether a limb goes back should depend on whether it still has substance, not on the hour. So the חצות line seems to have no case it could apply to.

steps.title: The answer begins: the case is still needed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins its answer with לא צריכא, saying there is a case where the חצות rule matters. The rest of the answer comes on the next amud.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is starting to answer the dilemma. It signals that it will describe a middle case where the time of night does matter, and the details continue on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase לא צריכא means the גמרא rejects both extremes from Step 17. It is about to point to a specific case that the משנה's rule fits.

keyTerms.meaning: No, it is necessary (for a specific case); the opening of an answer

phrases.english: No, it is necessary,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the answer to the dilemma in Step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Case limitation (a specific middle case, still to be named)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The חצות rule seemed to have no case it could apply to.
steps.terutzMaskana: There is a specific case where the time does matter; the details follow.
